title: Spanish food and restaurant words
examples: How do I ask for the menu in Spanish?
What do I say when I am finished eating?
What is a common Spanish dish I should know?

explain.say: Today we are learning words for food and restaurants in Spanish. You will learn how to order food like a local.
To ask for the menu, you can say, ¿Dónde está el menú? This means where is the menu.
If you want to order, you can say, Quiero una cerveza, which means I want a beer.
When you are finished, you ask for the bill by saying, La cuenta, por favor. This is very useful.
A very common Spanish dish is paella. It is a tasty rice dish often with seafood.
In real life, if you are at a restaurant, you might use all these phrases. You can start by asking for the menu first.

faq.q: What is the difference between 'Quiero' and 'Me gustaría'?
faq.a: 'Quiero' means I want, which is direct. 'Me gustaría' means I would like, which is a little softer way to ask.
asks: How do I ask politely for food?
Is 'Quiero' too direct for a restaurant?

faq.q: If I do not know the name of a dish, what can I say?
faq.a: You can point at the menu and say, ¿Qué es esto? This means what is this thing.
asks: Can I ask about food I cannot read?
What phrase do I use for unknown items?

faq.q: Do I need to learn words for drinks too?
faq.a: Yes, learning drinks like water or juice is very helpful for ordering everything.
asks: What are some common Spanish drinks?

faq.q: Is 'Gracias' used every time I speak Spanish?
faq.a: It is good to use it often, but you should also use 'Por favor' when you ask for something.
asks: When should I say thank you?

faq.a: It means the bill or the check, which is what you need to pay the restaurant.
asks: How do I ask for the bill in Spanish?
What is the Spanish word for the bill?

facts: Paella is a famous rice dish from Spain.
To ask for the menu, you say ¿Dónde está el menú?
To ask for the bill, you say La cuenta, por favor.
Quiero means I want, which is used when ordering.

quiz.say: If you want to order a soda, which phrase is best?
quiz.why: This uses the direct and clear phrase 'Quiero' which means I want.

wrong.0: This phrase is used only when you are ready to pay the bill.
wrong.1: This means thank you for the food, which is said after eating, not when ordering.
wrong.3: This question asks where the menu is, not what you want to order.

quiz.say: You have finished eating and need the bill. What should you say?
quiz.why: This is the specific polite phrase used to request the bill in Spanish.

wrong.0: This question asks for the menu, but you are asking for the bill.
wrong.1: While correct, 'La cuenta, por favor' is the standard polite request phrase.
wrong.3: Adiós means goodbye, which is used when leaving the restaurant.

quiz.say: You are at the table and need to see the menu. What do you ask?
quiz.why: This question directly asks for the location of the menu in Spanish.

wrong.1: This is grammatically okay but less natural than asking 'Where is the menu?'
wrong.2: This asks for the bill, which is the opposite of what you need.
wrong.3: This is a greeting, not a request for the menu.
